reason: A: the 'Find a Store' CTA is pushed into the top-left corner against the canvas edge, off the centred axis everything else uses, so the reading order runs backwards (CTA, then a tiny product, then the headline, with the GLACIER logo demoted below it); the can is shrunk to a sticker whose SOLSTICE label can't be read, and the legal line is jammed at the bottom edge. B: the elements share one centred axis, but the order is still inverted (the CTA sits above the headline, the logo sits under it, and the product is pushed to the bottom); the can is tiny and its label unreadable, it floats in a large empty lower area, and the legal line crowds right up under it. B is slightly tidier, but both fail on hierarchy and on keeping the product prominent.

A: the logo is blown up into a huge disc that competes with the headline, the dark header bar has turned into a stray block in the top-right corner, and the CTA sits above the headline and partly over the edge of that block, so the reading order is broken. 'Ships late June' is now as big as the body copy and the legal line is unreadably small. B has the same oversized logo and stray dark block, but it is worse: the CTA is shrunk to a tiny pill at the bottom next to the legal line, so the action is buried. A large empty area separates that pill from the text cluster, and there is an underline artifact on 'seaside k'. A at least keeps the CTA prominent.

A breaks the hierarchy: the subhead is blown up almost to headline size and competes with it, the headline is jammed against the top edge, and the CTA has shrunk to an unreadable pill in the bottom-left corner, cut off from the copy. B keeps the original's centred stack, colours and hierarchy cleanly, but it's just a scaled-down copy that wasn't rearranged for the wide banner: the subhead is small and borderline legible, and there's a lot of empty orange on both sides.

A: the GLACIER logo drops below the headline, which runs almost to the right edge; a huge dead band sits in the middle; the flavour pills are crammed into a ragged two-row cluster in reverse order, wedged between a CTA and legal line that crowd the bottom. B: logo also misplaced under the headline, which sits on the decorative circle, and the pills touch each other, vary in size (BLOOD ORANGE text is noticeably smaller) and run in reverse order, but the two-line headline, centred pill row and large CTA give clear hierarchy and even vertical rhythm.

A jams the NEW badge right against the end of the subline ('now.' nearly touches it), and its oversized Try It pill nearly fills the banner's height, so the right edge feels cramped. B keeps the original's left-to-right structure (can, headline, badge, CTA) with cleaner gaps, but the subline and the badge's 'NEW' text are tiny at 320x50 and the badge floats loosely in the middle.

A: the cream circle has come apart from the product and sits clipped in the bottom-left corner. The can's body is now the same orange as the background, so the product reads as an empty outline. The NEW badge floats alone in the top-right corner. Still, the right column (headline, then subcopy, then CTA) keeps a sensible order and alignment, even if it is loosely spaced. B: the product has shrunk to an unreadable thumbnail jammed against the left edge, and the cream circle sits clipped in the corner. The subcopy has fallen far below the headline, with the NEW badge and CTA strung across the middle between them, so the reading order is broken. The layout is mostly dead space.

A inverts the hierarchy: the quote has shrunk to a small single paragraph while the bold caps attribution 'THE GROVE TASTING TEAM' is as big or bigger and pulls focus. The can is oversized, centred and mostly off the backing circle, which is shoved to the bottom right, and the centred logo sits on the circle's edge. B keeps the original structure, the quote-over-attribution hierarchy and the left alignment. However, the circle is now enormous while the can inside it is small, so the 'SOLSTICE' label is nearly illegible, and the logo is tiny, leaving a lot of empty space in the left-centre.

A: the oversized SAVE 15% pill is the loudest thing on the canvas and pulls focus from the headline. The product bag is lost, leaving a blank blurred-brown rectangle in the middle-right with dead space after it. The tiny logo and bag thumbnail are jammed against the CTA, and the body copy wraps awkwardly. B: it has the same oversized badge, and its CTA has shrunk to a tiny, hard-to-read pill. The logo and bag are just specks beside it. Still, the headline and the one-line body read cleanly left to right, and the blurred image is only a thin sliver at the right edge, so B wastes less space than A's empty box.

Both lose the hero coffee bag: it shrinks to a thumbnail and leaves a huge empty blurred photo panel on the left. Both also put the CTA above the headline, which breaks the reading order. A's bag and logo are small but still recognisable, though they are pushed into the bottom corner next to a SAVE badge that floats loose, and the right-aligned CTA does not line up with the left text edge. B is worse: its bag and Q logo shrink to roughly 20px specks that cannot be read, so the brand is gone, and its centred CTA and centred badge sit on a different axis from the left-aligned headline.

A: the two-column layout (book left, copy right) suits the format and the headline leads. But the Inkwell & Lantern logo is shrunk to an unreadable smudge on the busy confetti strip. The '24 HOURS, 24 READERS' eyebrow has dropped below the body copy, and the body copy is as big as a subhead. The legal line leaves 'fund.' orphaned on its own line. B: the reading order is inverted, with the 'See the Schedule' CTA jammed against the top edge above the book and headline. The book is shrunk to a tiny icon, and the eyebrow is pushed below the body copy at a size that competes with the headline. The logo is an illegible speck in the bottom-left corner, and most of the confetti is gone, so the original's feel is lost.

A: the headline sits cleanly on one line and the logo→headline→CTA flow works. But the legal fine print is stacked above the supporting copy, so the reading order is inverted. A breaks the reading order badly. The cards are so small that their labels and prices are unreadable, so the pricing comparison is lost. B keeps the logo and headline at the top and puts Yearly and Family next to each other, but Monthly is left alone below the subhead. The cards are still too small to read, the price values are not legible, the subhead falls between the cards, and large dead gaps remain, so it is broken but a little more coherent than A.

A is mostly a scaled-down copy of the original: the can roundel is clipped at the bottom edge, the subline is close to illegible at 50px, and the NEW pill floats in the gap without belonging to anything. Still, its pill-shaped Try It CTA and its left-to-right banner order hold together. In B, Try It has become a squashed dark circle jammed against the top, bottom and right edges, and NEW is crammed against the end of the tagline so the two collide. A is basically the banner stretched out: the product can is tiny and stuck to the left edge, the cream circle has come loose and drifted to the bottom-left corner, the headline, badge and subcopy are spread far apart with big dead gaps, and the subcopy sits way below its headline. A is just the original shrunk into a centre column. B is broken: the dark logo sits on the dark navy and has almost disappeared, the white band is pushed off to the right with the CTA stuck inside it, the eyebrow 'LIMITED SUMMER RELEASE' has dropped below the body copy, and the type is jammed with no spacing, so the reading order and the layout both fall apart.

Both lose the dark header band, leaving a stray dark block in the top right, a loose orange divider and a white SOLSTICE wordmark that is almost invisible on cream. A: the badge is shrunk and wedged between the subhead and the legal text with no relation to either. A: the 'Longest Day Sale' ribbon is shrunk to a tiny strip under the CTA at the very bottom, so it reads last. A reflows the headline into a large, dominant 4-line stack with a readable subline, but the CTA is cut off from the group by a big gap (~140px vs ~70px headline-to-subline), and the gap below the CTA is cramped next to the empty top, so the stack looks bottom-heavy and loosely grouped. A: the CTA pill and LIMITED badge are stacked above the headline, which reverses the reading order. A: the flavour pills are crammed against the top edge, sit on top of the decorative circle and appear in reverse order; the GLACIER wordmark floats on its own between the headline and the subcopy with large empty gaps around it; the legal text runs into the bottom circle. A: the reading order is reversed, with the 'Shop Sale' CTA on the far left before the headline and the 'WEEKEND ONLY' eyebrow moved below the fine print. A splits the layout sensibly for the wide format, with a large bottle on the left and a strong headline/CTA stack on the right. A: the quote is only about 15px tall, the attribution is tiny, and the can is shrunk to a thumbnail sitting on top of a cropped circle. A has a sensible left-text/right-product split, but the SOLSTICE wordmark now sits below the headline and is almost as big as it, so the two compete. A keeps a logical logo→headline→subtext stack, but the legal line is nearly as large as the subtext, wraps to leave 'Co., 2026.' orphaned with a particle dot on it, the CTA is jammed against the right edge, and the sale ribbon sits stranded bottom-left with a tiny bottle at the left edge. A keeps the original's centered vertical stack and spacing, and works fine in the wider 614×768 canvas. A shrinks the 'Longest Day Sale' banner to an illegible tag, drops the product below the copy so the original order (brand, banner, product, headline) is reversed, sets the legal fine print almost as large as the subhead, and pushes the CTA nearly full-width against the bottom edge. A: the headline is jammed against the top edge and runs over a cropped circle fragment. A breaks the hero: the sage circle is split from the shoe and sits behind the headline and GROVE wordmark. The shoe floats in the bottom-right corner. A: the SOLSTICE wordmark sits below the headline, so the reading order is reversed, and it is spaced so wide that it competes with the headline. A shrinks the CTA 'Find It Near You' into a tiny pill jammed at the top with the badges, so the action is buried and comes first in reading order. A: the headline sits in the top third and the CTA pill is shrunk to a tiny bottom-left corner, with a huge dead orange void in between; the CTA and LIMITED badge are cut off from the message, and the badge has moved from before the button to after it, so the CTA looks like an afterthought. A is the better resize because its headline is far more readable at banner size. Both move the 'WEEKEND ONLY' eyebrow from above the headline to below the subcopy, which breaks the original reading order, and both shrink the legal line until it can barely be read. Both break the product graphic: the cream circle behind the can has come loose and sits clipped in the bottom-left corner, leaving an orange-on-orange can outline that barely shows. A shrinks the quote so far that the bold attribution outweighs it (hierarchy reversed), leaves 'soon.' orphaned on its own line, pushes the text almost to the left canvas edge, and places the logo awkwardly off-centre on the right; the small product floats above a large empty lower half. A: the dark header band has shrunk to an odd block in the top-right corner, so the SOLSTICE wordmark is white on cream and almost invisible; the orange divider rule has drifted off-axis to the right; and the copy is a small, narrow column that leaves big empty side areas. A jams the headline against the top-left edge with no margin, puts the SOLSTICE wordmark under the headline, reverses the pill order, and runs the tagline as tiny inline text after the pills.
